formulation.evidence: The postulate defines the Lorentzian static metric, Killing time and observer congruence, material EOS/state maps and SI units, positive compatible initial data, heat flux and conductivity, balance, insulated faces, support stress/current and zero-local-power condition.

scope.evidence: The physical_scope restricts the claim to one fixed-background, fixed-medium, supported parabolic heat branch. It excludes universal EOS claims, empirical realization, full Einstein-fluid dynamics, causal evolution, and finite propagation.

sources.evidence: The full Gourgoulhon and Borghini lecture-note PDFs were retrieved and their stated sections read. Coverage records exact locators, supported items, differences in frame conventions, and limits; neither source is used as proof of the adopted model.

non_derivation.evidence: The carrier labels the material, closure, coefficient, support and heat balance as adopted assumptions, has provenance.proof not-applicable, and reports no measurements or empirical evidence.

Choose positive lengths $L_1,L_2,L_3$, the rectangular box $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ of $\overline\Omega$. Let $N\in C^\infty(U,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $0<N_{\min}\leq N(x)\leq N_{\max}<\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$. On $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times U$, use $x^0=ct_K$, where $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and the fixed metric

$$g=-N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2.$$

The coordinates $x^i$ and lengths $L_i$ are measured in metres, $t_K$ in seconds, and the lapse $N$ is dimensionless. The metric is independent of $x^0$ and has no time-space cross terms; this is the static background in this model. Give $M$ time orientation $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$. Then $\xi$ is a future timelike Killing field, $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is the smooth future unit timelike observer congruence in the conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Here a frame means this vector field and its pointwise rest spaces, not a coordinate chart or tetrad. The material is held at rest in this congruence; no flow evolution is included. The scalar $T>0$ is proper temperature in kelvins, and $\vartheta:=NT$ is the Killing-normalized (redshifted) temperature of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]; this definition alone does not assert that $\vartheta$ is constant.

Adopt the fixed-composition material branch of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] with constants $C_V,n_0,T_{\rm ref}>0$, $\sigma_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R$, and $e_0\in\mathbb R$. The units are $C_V$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}K^{-1}}$, $n_0$ in $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $T_{\rm ref}$ in kelvins, $\sigma_{\rm ref}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and $e_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. Put $c_v=C_V/n_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$ and choose the state function on $X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ to be

$$e(v,\sigma_p)=c_vT_{\rm ref}\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma_p-\sigma_{\rm ref}}{c_v}\right)+e_0,$$

independent of the rest volume per marker $v$. For a given positive $T$, set $v=1/n_0$ and $\sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$. For this branch define $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\epsilon=ne$, $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e$, and $p=-\partial_ve$, using the units of [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and the adopted material convention of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. These maps give $n=n_0$, $p=0$, $\epsilon=C_VT+n_0e_0$, and $s=n_0\sigma_{\rm ref}+C_V\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$. These assignments describe the selected model only; they do not assert a measured equation of state.

Take an admissible initial redshifted-temperature profile $\vartheta_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ with constants $0<m_0\leq M_0<\infty$ such that $m_0\leq\vartheta_0\leq M_0$, and require a $C^2$ extension $\widetilde\vartheta_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with the same bounds, period $2L_i$ in each coordinate $x^i$, and evenness under each reflection $x^i\mapsto-x^i$. Its even periodic extension makes the normal derivative vanish at both faces in each coordinate once evolved smoothly. The initial proper temperature is $T(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$.

On $O=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$, adopt the following restricted heat branch of [[post-tgr-first-order-dissipation]]. The physical heat-flux field $q$ is spatial, has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, and has constitutive coefficient $\kappa_{\rm th}=A_0/N$ for a constant $A_0>0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$. With $\nabla_x$ the Euclidean spatial gradient, its specified static heat law, local energy balance, and insulated-face condition are

$$q=-\kappa_{\rm th}(\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N),\qquad \kappa_{\rm th}=\frac{A_0}{N},\qquad NC_V\partial_{t_K}T+\operatorname{div}_x(N^2q)=0,\qquad N^2q\cdot\nu=0\ \text{on each face},$$

where $\operatorname{div}_x$ is Euclidean divergence and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a box face. The adopted first-order closure specializes to this lapse-gradient form in the selected static frame; it is not inferred from an experiment. Since $N$ is time independent, $\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N=N^{-1}\nabla_x\vartheta$, so this coefficient choice gives $N^2q=-A_0\nabla_x\vartheta$ and diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$.

For the material stress/current in this selected branch put $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J^a=n_0u^a$, and

$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b.$$

Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in $\mathrm{Pa}$. The external support is the force-density field $f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$, in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, required to hold the medium on the fixed background. Require $u_bf^b=0$: the support may supply spatial force but no local power. This is a supported material model, not source-free full matter dynamics. Its entropy current is $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$; this postulate alone does not assert an entropy inequality.

This is an adopted effective parabolic model. It asserts no Einstein equation, no general relativistic-fluid initial-value theorem, no finite propagation speed, and no universal material law. It supplies no experiment, measurement, empirical premise, or evidence that a physical medium realizes the model.

On an open region of the smooth spacetime of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], take a separately specified material/current model in its declared smooth regime. Its entropy current is a supplied $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ of the type and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Adopt the local admissibility condition

$$\nabla_aS^a\geq 0$$

throughout that region. This inequality is a physical restriction on the chosen model and current; it is not a construction of an undefined constitutive current. Each application must state its current, regime, boundary/exchange data, and any source or sink terms it includes.

The inequality is not deduced from Lorentzian geometry, the local state function, or finite data. It does not assert statistical thermalization, a universal microscopic $H$-theorem, entropy-area identification, or a generalized second law. Romatschke's cited calculation is restricted to a specified conformal-fluid model and itself records the absence of experimental verification known to that author; that source limitation does not turn this postulate into an observed law. No experimental observation or uncertainty is supplied by this item.

Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with $L_i>0$, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$. $$

$$
where $x^i$ are measured in metres, $t_K$ in seconds, and $N$ is dimensionless. By [[def-gr-killing-field]], a Killing field is one satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, where $\mathcal L_\xi g=\frac d{dt}|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g$ for the local flow $\Phi_t$ of $\xi$. Thus $\xi$ is a future timelike Killing field, $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is the smooth future unit timelike observer congruence of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]; here this congruence means the unit timelike vector field, not a coordinate chart. Write $\nabla_x$, $\operatorname{div}_x$, $\nu$, and $dx$ for the Euclidean spatial gradient, divergence, outward unit normal, and three-dimensional Lebesgue volume on the box, and set $|\Omega|:=\int_\Omega1\,dx=L_1L_2L_3$. For scalar fields on $\Omega$, $L^2(\Omega)$ and its norm use this measure.

For $t_K>0$ use the open domain $O=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Spatial vectors such as $q$ are extended to spacetime with zero $x^0$ component.

Fix constants $C_V,n_0,A_0,T_{\rm ref}>0$, a reference entropy $\sigma_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R$, and a reference energy $e_0\in\mathbb R$. Their units are $C_V$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}K^{-1}}$, $n_0$ in $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $A_0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $T_{\rm ref}$ in kelvins, $\sigma_{\rm ref}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and $e_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. Define the derived per-marker heat capacity $c_v=C_V/n_0$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and the local mathematical material state function on $X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ by
$$
e(v,\sigma_p)=c_vT_{\rm ref}\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma_p-\sigma_{\rm ref}}{c_v}\right)+e_0,
$$
independent of $v$. For a positive proper temperature $T$, set $\sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$ and $v=1/n_0$. The state definitions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] give $n=n_0$, $p=0$, $\epsilon=C_VT+n_0e_0$, and $s=n_0\sigma_{\rm ref}+C_V\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$.

Let $\vartheta_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ satisfy $0<m_0\le\vartheta_0\le M_0$ and admit a $C^2$ extension $\widetilde\vartheta_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with the same bounds, period $2L_i$ in coordinate $x^i$, and evenness under $x^i\mapsto-x^i$ for each $i$. These conditions make the extension even about every face $x^i=0,L_i$. Set $T_0=\vartheta_0/N$. Define the physical heat flux, conductivity, static heat balance, and insulated-face condition by
$$
q=-\kappa_{\rm th}(\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N),\qquad \kappa_{\rm th}=A_0/N,\qquad NC_V\partial_{t_K}T+\operatorname{div}_x(N^2q)=0,\qquad N^2q\cdot\nu=0\ \text{on each face},
$$
where $q$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, $\kappa_{\rm th}$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a face. In the entropy identity use zero particle diffusion and zero shear and bulk viscosity, $V=0$ and $\eta=\zeta_{\rm b}=0$, so $\Pi=0$ and $\pi^{ab}=0$. The thermal diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. There is a unique solution $T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)$, where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces, satisfying the heat balance, the face condition, and the initial condition $T(0,x)=T_0(x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$. It is given by
$$\vartheta(t_K,x):=N(x)T(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad \Gamma(z,t)=(4\pi t)^{-3/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4t)},\quad z\in\mathbb R^3,\ t>0.$$
Thus $T=\vartheta/N$. It satisfies $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, $\partial_\nu\vartheta=0$ on each face, and $m_0\le\vartheta\le M_0$.

For this solution set $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J=n_0u$, and
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b,\qquad f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}.
$$
Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, $\mathsf T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $f$ has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Then $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $u_bf^b=0$: $f$ is an explicitly defined external support that supplies no local power. The entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, with
$$
\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\ge0.
$$
The lapse-weighted energy $\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N\epsilon\,dx$ is constant in $\mathrm{J}$. If $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$, then
$$
\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
$$
Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to $T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta/N$. Since $N T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta>0$, the inverse-temperature vector $\beta=u/(k_BT_{\rm eq})$, for $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, is Killing by [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]]. This is a mathematical solution of the specified fixed-background, supported first-order heat model; it asserts no Einstein equation, general dissipative-fluid initial-value theorem, or finite propagation speed.

derivations.claim: The adopted static flux law gives q=−A0 N^(−2)∇x(NT); therefore N²q=−A0∇x vartheta. Since N is time independent, the balance becomes CV ∂tK vartheta=A0 Δx vartheta and the insulated condition is ∂nu vartheta=0. The material and support conventions match the exact mathematical supplier.

The C² periodic initial extension is bounded and uniformly continuous and is positive and even at each face. Together with Li,A0,CV,Nmin>0, these are the exact inputs of the current mathematical result. Its conditional statement and proof yield the unique heat solution, Gaussian formula, bounds, energy conservation, entropy rate and exponential redshifted-temperature estimate.

The entropy current and its interpretation match the physical model. The local admissibility condition is an adopted physical premise; independently the mathematical supplier gives the global rate with integrand A0|∇vartheta|²/vartheta², which is nonnegative. It also supplies conservation of the lapse-weighted energy.

Because N≥Nmin>0, |T−vartheta_bar/N|≤Nmin^(−1)|vartheta−vartheta_bar| pointwise. Taking the stated L² norm and applying the mathematical exponential estimate proves convergence of proper temperature to the positive profile vartheta_bar/N; multiplication by N shows redshifted temperature tends to the constant vartheta_bar.

where $q$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, $\kappa_{\rm th}$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a face. In the entropy identity use zero particle diffusion and zero shear and bulk viscosity, $V=0$ and $\eta=\zeta_{\rm b}=0$, so $\Pi=0$ and $\pi^{ab}=0$. The thermal diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. There is a unique solution $T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)$, where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces, satisfying the heat balance, the face condition, and the initial condition $T(0,x)=T_0(x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$. It is given by
$$\vartheta(t_K,x):=N(x)T(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad \Gamma(z,t)=(4\pi t)^{-3/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4t)},\quad z\in\mathbb R^3,\ t>0.$$
Thus $T=\vartheta/N$. It satisfies $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, $\partial_\nu\vartheta=0$ on each face, and $m_0\le\vartheta\le M_0$.

For this solution set $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J=n_0u$, and
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b,\qquad f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}.
$$
Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, $\mathsf T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $f$ has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Then $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $u_bf^b=0$: $f$ is an explicitly defined external support that supplies no local power. The entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, with
$$
\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\ge0.
$$
The lapse-weighted energy $\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N\epsilon\,dx$ is constant in $\mathrm{J}$. If $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$, then
$$
\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
$$
Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to $T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta/N$. Since $N T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta>0$, the inverse-temperature vector $\beta=u/(k_BT_{\rm eq})$, for $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, is Killing by [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]]. This is a mathematical solution of the specified fixed-background, supported first-order heat model; it asserts no Einstein equation, general dissipative-fluid initial-value theorem, or finite propagation speed.

Use the fixed static box, positive bounded lapse $N$, constants, material state function, observer field, heat flux, support, initial-data class, and SI conventions of [[post-tgr-supported-static-heat-model]]. Let $\widetilde\vartheta_0$ be its positive $C^2$ even periodic extension, and define $|\Omega|=L_1L_2L_3$, $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$, and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$. Use Euclidean Lebesgue volume $dx$ and the associated $L^2(\Omega)$ norm. Then the model has a unique solution

$$T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega),$$

where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces at positive times. With $\vartheta=NT$ and $\Gamma(z,\tau)=(4\pi\tau)^{-3/2}\exp(-|z|^2/(4\tau))$ for $z\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\tau>0$, the solution is

$$\vartheta(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad T=\frac{\vartheta}{N}.$$

$$\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N(x)\epsilon(t_K,x)\,dx$$

is constant. For the entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$, the exact model rate is

$$\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\geq0.$$

Moreover,

$$\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq\exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to the positive proper-temperature profile $T_{\rm eq}(x)=\overline\vartheta/N(x)$, while the redshifted temperature $NT$ converges to the constant $\overline\vartheta$. These are conditional predictions of the adopted model. They do not establish that a real material obeys the postulates, and they do not assert a full Einstein-fluid solution, causal or stable relativistic-fluid evolution, or finite propagation speed. No empirical data are used.

derivations.claim: The cosine extends smoothly, evenly and periodically, with bounds vartheta_bar−|delta| and vartheta_bar+|delta|. The strict delta bound gives positive admissible data. The cosine averages to zero over (0,L1), so the initial redshifted-temperature mean is vartheta_bar.

Direct differentiation gives the heat equation and initial trace. The x1 derivative vanishes at both endpoints and the other coordinate derivatives vanish identically, so all faces are insulated. Uniqueness identifies the displayed mode with the physical model solution.

The exponential mode tends to zero. Division by the fixed positive lapse gives the proper-temperature limit; nonconstant N makes that limit nonconstant. Direct integration of cos² over the box gives the exact L² norm |delta|sqrt(|Omega|/2)e^(−rtK).
